title: Meat loaf made with beef and pork

content.title: About
content.content: Meat loaf made with beef and pork is a baked dish prepared from a mixture of ground beef and pork, combined with eggs, breadcrumbs, spices, and sometimes vegetables. It has a dense texture, savory flavor, and is often served in slice form.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally the loaf is baked in a large loaf pan and then sliced into portions.
In the United States it is commonly topped with a tomato‑based glaze or brown‑sugar glaze.
There are countless variations – cheese, mushrooms, vegetables, even dried fruit are added in different recipes.
The dish became popular in military mess halls because it is easy to prepare and stores well when kept properly.
In some regions the loaf is nicknamed “meat cake” because of its shape and texture.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beef and pork provide high‑quality complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed and supports oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is a good source of B12, B6 and niacin, which help nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Source of zinc
items.content: Zinc from meat supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The fat and calorie content make meat loaf a convenient energy source for active individuals.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Excess saturated fat can raise blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Many recipes call for a generous amount of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor pathogenic bacteria; cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some versions contain dairy or gluten, which can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the meat loaf thinly and serve hot or cold. It can be eaten on its own, in sandwiches, alongside vegetables, mashed potatoes, or with a sauce of your choice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked loaf in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized pieces – up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 71 °C before serving.
